html:
SMTO-GWT-0006 — SMTO got a message from the Gateway it couldn't trust

GUID: 1f1ab5e6-c660-48cd-94ed-3eee7c4c8808
Slug: gateway-protocol-error
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • A message between SMTO and the computer came back garbled, too large, or in an unexpected form. If a task was running, SMTO can't tell whether its last step happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task and read its latest steps, or look on that computer, to see whether the change you asked for (a file, a command, a setting) already happened. SMTO couldn't read the reply, so the work may have finished even though it looks failed.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, expand the Gateway's row, and select Check for updates in Software updates. If an update is offered, install it once nothing is running there. A Gateway and SMTO on very different versions can send each other messages the other can't read.
  3. Select Edit and make sure Host and Port point to the Gateway itself, not to another program or web proxy on that computer. If a different program answers at that address, its replies make no sense to SMTO.
  4. Only if you confirmed the earlier step did not happen, run it again. Repeating a step that already ran could make the same change twice.

What success looks like

  • Select Check connection shows Connected, and the task's next step completes with a normal result.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that computer. Don't repeat a change on that computer until you know whether the first attempt went through.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway request or reply failed protocol validation (malformed or non-object JSON, size, identity or receipt checks); whether execution started depends on the failing phase.

What this means

  • A Gateway message failed its JSON, object-shape, size, identity or receipt contract. Producers include discovery, request admission, execution replies and stream events, so this category does not establish whether execution started. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • A Gateway message failed its JSON, object-shape, size, identity or receipt contract. Producers include discovery, request admission, execution replies and stream events, so this category does not establish whether execution started.

How to diagnose it

  • Determine whether the rejected message was a discovery result, an incoming request or an execution receipt; inspect retained phase and operation identity.

How to fix it

  • Read failure_phase and the message in Technical details to see whether discovery, admission, an execution reply or a stream event failed. Compare the Gateway and Server versions and make sure nothing between them (proxy, other service on the port) rewrites traffic; if the failure came after dispatch, check the operation's job status or receipt on the Gateway before sending any further change.
  • Check the failing protocol and Gateway version. If an operation may have started, inspect its existing state before sending another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Discovery or admission validates, or the original execution is reconciled to a trustworthy receipt before another mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
  • SMTO-GWT-0013 — Gateway identity changed
  • SMTO-GWT-0005 — Gateway unauthorized
  • SMTO-GWT-0007 — SMTO couldn't confirm the computer got your stop or input request
